evidence.source: REM-57 gate found a real fail-OPEN adoption path in chooseProjection: `data` was re-redacted but the remote projection's `sections`, `coverage` and the returned `snapshot` were copied VERBATIM, and panel.js feeds those sections straight into PROJECTION.sections and the dashboard cards. So an observer-snapshot.json written by an older or buggy app build could carry a fabricated `reminderHealth` section, reminder fields smuggled inside a known section (reminderBody / occurrenceId / ghToken) and a raw coverage path holding the user's own reminder title into the panel; REM-26 missed it because it only tested the snapshot it built itself. Mirror sections are now always rebuilt locally, only the five raw-derived sections (dailyPhoto, therapyProvenance, profileProgress, notificationTimeline, externalSources) are adopted and are recursively stripped of secret/blob/reminder-namespace keys, unknown section keys are dropped, remote coverage is re-classified with reminder entries masked, and the returned snapshot carries metadata plus sanitized payload only; rich raw-derived values (thoughtCount, responseCount, lifecycle counters) survive and chosen.adoption reports the decision. DECISION REM-ADR-021: the panel reminder surface stays a no-op on separate feature, operator and privacy grounds; the minimum redacted aggregate was rejected; the only exception is REM-53's fixed lifecycle event summary. panel.js was a deliberate no-op because the boundary belongs in the pure adapter every consumer shares. POST-CLOSURE CORRECTION (080132d): a full-application audit found the `projection_stale` branch still returned the remote projection verbatim in the `snapshot` field — sanitization had only covered the `ready` branch and the fixture missed it because it drove the stale branch with a clean self-built snapshot. No DOM leak (panel.js only assigns PROJECTION.snapshot, never reads it for render) but the untrusted payload lived in panel memory and in the panelSig() serialization. The stale branch now returns diagnostic metadata only; the gate drives all six branches with a hostile projection and also proves fail-closed no-throw behaviour for malformed shapes
